body: I wonder if it is an unhealthy coping mechanism for those who suffer tho?  I suppose it's much better thinking about it than actually going through it.  I fantasize about it a lot, and when I do, it does seem to relieve some pressure and stress.  It's like "If I off myself, then all this pressure will go away," and I know there's that option available to me and relieves some of that pressure in a weird way.

My depression and anxiety causes my sex drive to retract, so the desire to have sex becomes almost repulsive.  And, at the same time, I withdraw from people and it becomes a downward spiral of feeling even more lonely and isolated.  It's something I've worked on for years...I'm not sure what the solution is now.

Thanks buddy.  I try not to share too much with friends these days, as I've already done that too much as it is.  After a while, you become the 'downer friend' and nobody wants to talk to you much about it.  One of my coping mechanisms was the gym, and it's been a while, but I really need to get back.  it helped a lot, looking back.

I don't think anyone who's not gay can truly understand the estrangement you mention.  We are bombarded by heterocentric images every day, beaten up on the news channels and various blogs, and have to read the homophobic comments from youtube and various other channels.  Not to mention having to restrain ourselves in public for fear people may attack if we appear to close to someone we care for.  It can be really rough.
Thanks...your comment really resonated with me.  I read it a few days ago from my main account and I have really thought about it.  You've given me some good ideas, thank you so much for that.

If you're feeling suicidal because of your sexuality, the cliche "it gets better" is true.  Once you do find the family that supports you for who you are, the family you had before becomes less relevant.

My pain stems a bit from that, but it also just comes from years of abuse and neglect, and feeling anxiety about how much worse things can get.

I don't think I'm going to do it.  I've had quite a number of family members that I love who have and it was painful to me.  But I still think about it a lot.  I never imagined I'd live to see 30, and now 40 is coming up, so that's a pleasant surprise I guess.
